In this section, we report the PCFGs used in the experiment "Decoupling contextual gender information from static gender associations." We categorise feminine and masculine nouns into four groups based on their appearance in gendered (G) or gender-ambiguous (A) contexts within lm_train and whether they are present in a gendered context (G) in probe_train or remain unseen (U) in this set. The results presented in Table 1 concern exclusively nouns in the latter category. Thus, any gender information detected by the linguistic probe at inference time is encoded in the LM's representation and not merely memorised by the probe.

The following PCFG is used to generate lm_train.

$$
S \rightarrow N P V P ^ {\prime \prime}. ^ {\prime \prime} [ 1. 0 ]
$$

$$
P P \rightarrow \text {P R E P N} [ 1. 0 ]
$$

$$
V P \rightarrow V E R B [ 0. 5 ] \mid V E R B N P [ 0. 5 ]
$$

$$
N P \rightarrow N P G e n d [ 0. 4 ] \mid N P A m b [ 0. 4 ]
$$

$$
N P \rightarrow N P P P [ 0. 2 ]
$$

$$
N P G e n d \rightarrow D E T F e m n p G e n d F e m [ 0. 5 ]
$$

$$
N P G e n d \rightarrow D E T M a s c n p G e n d M a s c [ 0. 5 ]
$$

$$
\mathrm {n p G e n d F e m} \rightarrow \mathrm {N O U N F e m G e n d} [ 0. 4 ]
$$

$$
\mathrm {n p G e n d F e m} \rightarrow \mathrm {A D J F e m N O U N F e m G e n d} [ 0. 3 ]
$$

$$
\mathrm {n p G e n d F e m} \rightarrow \text {N O U N F e m G e n d A D J F e m [ 0 . 3 ]}
$$

$$
n p G e n d M a s c - > N O U N M a s c G e n d [ 0. 4 ]
$$

$$
\mathsf {n p G e n d M a s c} \rightarrow \mathsf {A D J M a s c N O U N M a s c G e n d} [ 0. 3 ]
$$

$$
n p G e n d M a s c \rightarrow N O U N M a s c G e n d A D J M a s c [ 0. 3 ]
$$

$$
N P A m b \rightarrow D E T E p i c n p A m b F e m [ 0. 5 ]
$$

$$
N P A m b \rightarrow D E T E p i c n p A m b M a s c [ 0. 5 ]
$$

$$
n p A m b F e m \rightarrow N O U N F e m A m b [ 0. 4 ]
$$

$$
n p A m b F e m \rightarrow A D J E p i c N O U N F e m A m b [ 0. 3 ]
$$

$$
n p A m b F e m \rightarrow N O U N F e m A m b A D J E p i c [ 0. 3 ]
$$

$$
n p A m b M a s c \rightarrow N O U N M a s c A m b [ 0. 4 ]
$$

$$
n p A m b M a s c \rightarrow D A J E p i c N O U N M a s c A m b [ 0. 3 ]
$$

$$
n p A m b M a s c \rightarrow N O U N M a s c A m b A D J E p i c [ 0. 3 ]
$$

$$
N O U N F e m A m b \rightarrow N O U N F e m A G [ 0. 5 ]
$$

$$
N O U N F e m A m b \rightarrow N O U N F e m A U [ 0. 5 ]
$$

```txt
NOUNMascAmb -> NOUNMascAG [0.5]  
NOUNMascAmb -> NOUNMascAU [0.5]  
NOUNFemGend -> NOUNFemGG [0.5]  
NOUNFemGend -> NOUNFemGU [0.5]  
NOUNMascGend -> NOUNMascGG [0.5]  
NOUNMascGend -> NOUNMascGU [0.5] 
```

The PCFG presented below is employed for generating probe_train.

```json
S->NPVP"."[1.0] 
```

```txt
PP->PREP NP[1.0]  
VP->VERB[0.5] | VERB NP[0.5] 
```

```txt
NP->NPGend[0.8] | NP PP[0.20] 
```

```txt
NPGend -> DETFem npGendFem [0.5]  
NPGend -> DETMasc npGendMasc [0.5]  
npGendFem -> NOUNFemGend [0.4]  
npGendFem -> ADJFem NOUNFemGend [0.3]  
npGendFem -> NOUNFemGend ADJFem [0.3]  
npGendMasc -> NOUNMascGend [0.4]  
npGendMasc -> ADJMasc NOUNMascGend [0.3]  
npGendMasc -> NOUNMascGend ADJMasc [0.3] 
```

```txt
NOUNFemGend -> NOUNFemGG [0.5]  
NOUNFemGend -> NOUNFemAG [0.5]  
NOUNMascGend -> NOUNMascGG [0.  
NOUNMascGend -> NOUNMascAG [0. 
```

To create probe_test, we use variations of the following rules. Placeholder X denotes the context in which a noun appears in lm_train and can assume the values G or A. On the other hand, Y represents the context in probe_train and can be either G or U.

```json
S->NPVP"."[1.0] 
```

```txt
PP->PREP NP[1.0]  
VP->VERB[0.5] | VERB NP[0.5] 
```

```txt
NOUNFem -> NOUNFemXY [1.0]  
NOUNMasc -> NOUNMascXY [1.0] 
```

If the selected noun category is to be tested in gendered contexts during inference, the following rules are also added to the PCFG.

```txt
NP->NPGend[0.8] | NP PP[0.20] 
```

```txt
NPGend -> DETFem npGendFem [0.5]  
NPGend -> DETMasc npGendMasc [0.5]  
npGendFem -> NOUNFem [0.4] 
```

```txt
npGendFem -> ADJFem NOUNFem [0.3]  
npGendFem -> NOUNFem ADJFem [0.3]  
npGendMasc -> NOUNMasc [0.4]  
npGendMasc -> ADJMasc NOUNMasc [0.3]  
npGendMasc -> NOUNMasc ADJMasc [0.3] 
```

If the nouns are to appear in gender-ambiguous contexts, on the other hand, the rules that follow are applied.

```txt
NP->NPAmb[0.8] | NP PP[0.20] 
```

```txt
NPAmb -> DETEpic npAmbFem [0.5]  
NPAmb -> DETEpic npAmbMasc [0.5]  
npAmbFem -> NOUNFem [0.4]  
npAmbFem -> ADJEpic NOUNFem [0.3]  
npAmbFem -> NOUNFem ADJEpic [0.3]  
npAmbMasc -> NOUNMasc [0.4]  
npAmbMasc -> ADJEpic NOUNMasc [0.3]  
npAmbMasc -> NOUNMasc ADJEpic [0.3] 
```

In this section, we report the PCFGs used in the experiment "Assignment of gender to epicene nouns."

```json
S->NPVP"."[1.0] 
```

```txt

```

```txt
NP->NPGend[0.4] | NPAmb[0.4] NP->NP PP [0.20] 
```

```txt

NPAmb -> DETepic ADJEpic NOUN [0.3]  
NPAmb -> DETepic NOUN ADJEpic [0.3]

NOUN -> NOUN25 [0.1] | NOUN50 [0.1]
```


The subsequent PCFG is used for generating probe_test. The placeholders Y and X can be substituted with specific values to represent the noun category being tested and the context in which these nouns should appear, respectively. For Y, the options include Fem, Masc, 25, 50, or 75. As for X, it can be replaced with Fem, Masc, or Amb.

```txt
S -> NP VP ". ." [1.0]  
PP -> PREP NP [1.0]  
VP -> VERB [0.5] | VERB NP [0.5]  
NP -> NPX [0.80] | NP PP [0.20]  
NPAmb -> DETEpic NOUN [0.4]  
NPAmb -> DETEpic ADJEpic NOUN [0.4]  
NPAmb -> DETEpic NOUN ADJEpic [0.4]  
NPFem -> DETFem NOUN [0.4]  
NPFem -> DETFem ADJFem NOUN [0.4]  
NPFem -> DETFem NOUN [0.4]  
NPMasc -> DETMasc NOUN [0.4]  
NPMasc -> DETMasc ADJMasc NOUN [0.4]  
NPMasc -> DETMasc NOUN ADJMasc [0.4]  
NOUN -> NOUNY [1.0] 
```
